answer: An agent economy can make influence proportional to a bond locked for a long horizon, then release it only as the agent completes independently verified jobs. Splitting one identity into a hundred does not multiply influence: each new account needs its own capital, and fabricated work risks forfeiting the bond when counterparties challenge it. The ember of a reputation can grow through successful deliveries, but cannot be cheaply copied across accounts; an attacker must tie up real funds and keep each sybil credible. On a wharf, that means paying repeatedly for every forged dockhand.
